edition.locus: De Trinitate XXV (mortuus pro nobis; death vs body not Word; immortalitas)

source_text: XXV. 1. Ergo, inquiunt, si Christus non homo est tantum, sed et Deus, Christum autem refert scriptura mortuum pro nobis et resuscitatum, iam docet nos scriptura credere Deum mortuum. Aut si Deus non moritur, Christus autem mortuus refertur, non erit Christus Deus, quoniam Deus non potest accipi mortuus. 2. Si umquam intellegerent aut intellexissent quod legunt, numquam tam periculose omnino loquerentur. Sed erroris semper est abrupta dementia et non est nouum, si usque ad periculosa descendunt qui fidem legitimam reliquerunt. 3. Si enim scriptura proponeret Christum tantummodo Deum et nulla in illo fragilitatis humanae sociatio esset permixta, merito illorum hic aliquid ualuisset sermo contortus: 'si Christus Deus, Christus autem mortuus, ergo mortuus est Deus'. 4. Sed cum non tantummodo illum, ut ostendimus iam frequenter, Deum, sed et hominem scriptura constituat, consequens est, quod immortale est, incorruptum mansisse teneatur. Quis enim non intellegat quod impassibilis sit diuinitas, passibilis uero sit humana fragilitas? 5. Cum ergo tam ex eo quod Deus est, quam etiam ex illo quod homo est Christus intellegatur esse permixtus et esse sociatus, Verbum enim caro factum est et habitauit in nobis, quis non sine ullo magistro atque interprete ex sese facile cognoscat non illud in Christo mortuum esse quod Deus est, sed illud in illo mortuum esse quod homo est? 6. Quid enim si diuinitas in Christo non moritur, sed carnis solius substantia exstinguitur, quando et in ceteris hominibus, qui non sunt caro tantummodo, sed caro et anima, caro quidem sola incursum interitus mortisque patitur, extra leges autem interitus et mortis anima incorrupta cernatur? 7. Hoc enim et ipse Dominus hortans nos ad martyrium et ad contemptum omnis humanae potestatis aiebat: Ne timueritis eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem occidere non possunt. 8. Quodsi anima immortalis occidi aut interfici non potest in quouis alio, licet corpus et caro sola possit interfici, quanto magis utique uerbum Dei et Deus in Christo interfici omnino non potuit, cum caro sola et corpus occisum sit? 9. Si enim hanc habet generositatem immortalitatis anima in quouis homine, ut non possit interfici, multo magis hanc habet potestatem generositas uerbi Dei, ut non possit occidi. Nam si potestas hominum ad interficiendam sacram Dei potestatem et si crudelitas humana ad interficiendam animam deficit, multo magis ad Dei uerbum interficiendum deficere debebit. Nam cum ipsa anima, quae per Dei uerbum facta est, ab hominibus non occiditur, multo magis utique uerbum Dei perimi non posse credetur. 10. Et si plus non potest hominum cruenta saeuitia aduersus homines quam ut tantummodo corpus occidat, quanto magis utique in Christo non ualebit quam ut item tantummodo corpus occidat, ut dum per haec colligitur non nisi hominem in Christo interfectum, appareat ad mortalitatem sermonem in loco non esse deductum. 11. Nam si Abraham et Isaac et Iacob, quos homines tantummodo constat fuisse, manifestum est uiuere — omnes enim, inquit, illi uiuunt Deo nec mors in illis animam perimit, quae corpora ipsa dissoluit; ius enim suum exercere potuit in corpora, in animas exercere non ualuit; aliud enim in illis mortale et ideo mortuum, aliud in illis immortale et ideo intellegitur non exstinctum; ob quam causam uiuere Deo pronuntiati et dicti sunt —, multo magis utique mors in Christo aduersum solam materiam corporis potuit ualere, aduersus diuinitatem sermonis non potuit se exercere. Frangitur enim potestas mortis ubi intercedit auctoritas immortalitatis.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, they say, if Christ is not man only but also God, and Scripture reports Christ dead for us and raised, already Scripture teaches us to believe God dead. Or if God does not die, and Christ is reported dead, Christ will not be God. If they ever understood what they read, they would never speak so dangerously. If Scripture set forth Christ as God only with no mixture of human frailty, their speech would have some force. But when Scripture sets forth both man and God in Christ, death could prevail only against the matter of the body, not against the divinity of the Word. For death's power is broken where immortality's authority intervenes.
pass_b_english: Therefore, they say, if Christ is not man only but also God, and Scripture reports Christ dead for us and raised, already Scripture teaches us to believe God dead. Or if God does not die, and Christ is reported dead, Christ will not be God, since God cannot be received as dead. If they ever understood or had understood what they read, they would never speak so dangerously at all. But it is always the steep madness of error, and it is not new if those who have left lawful faith descend even to dangerous things. If Scripture set forth Christ as God only and no fellowship of human frailty were mixed in him, their speech here would deservedly have some force. But since from the divine writings both are brought together in Christ — that he is and God and man — death is referred to man in Christ, resurrection is also shown referred to man. As in those who have departed, death could exercise force against souls only so far; for something in them was mortal and therefore dead, something immortal and therefore understood not extinguished — for which cause they are pronounced and said to live to God — much more could death in Christ prevail only against the matter of the body; against the divinity of the Word it could not exercise itself. For death's power is broken where immortality's authority intervenes.

lemmas.sense: Christ dead for us without God dying as God
death prevails only against bodily matter
raising also referred with the man

choices.choose: Christ God and man died for us in the body; the Word's divinity did not die
reject: either God died as God or Christ is not God
choices.why: Mors aduersum solam materiam corporis; aduersus diuinitatem sermonis non.

choices.choose: death's power breaks where immortality's authority intervenes
reject: death extinguishes the whole Christ without remainder
choices.why: Frangitur potestas mortis ubi intercedit auctoritas immortalitatis.
